title: API stability policy
text: 1.0.0, kernR adopts strict frozen-API additive evolution — policy glmnet, mgcv, long-lived statistical inference packages: Signatures exported functions never change backwards-incompatible way across major versions. New capability arrives via new entry points (new exports), never via changes existing ones. existing function genuinely needs retired, marked lifecycle::deprecate_warn(), kept ≥ 2 minor versions, promoted lifecycle::deprecate_stop() ≥ 1 minor version, removed next major release. Successors signposted deprecation message. policy chosen kernR provides hypothesis-testing machinery downstream consumers (PESTO ⇄ kernR ⇄ proxymix chain; agricultural pipeline code; methods-paper supplementary material) wire long-lived calibration verdict workflows. Silent breakage across versions defeat contract.

code: set.seed(42L) n_var <- 400L x_var <- matrix(rnorm(n_var * 2L), n_var, 2L) t_var <- rbinom(n_var, 1L, plogis(0.3 * x_var[, 1L])) noise_treated <- rnorm(n_var, sd = 2.5) noise_control <- rnorm(n_var, sd = 1) noise_treated <- noise_treated - mean(noise_treated[t_var == 1L]) noise_control <- noise_control - mean(noise_control[t_var == 0L]) y_var <- (1L - t_var) * noise_control + t_var * noise_treated +   0.5 * x_var[, 1L] lm_variance <- lm(y_var ~ t_var + x_var) lm_effect <- coef(lm_variance)[["t_var"]] lm_p <- summary(lm_variance)$coefficients["t_var", "Pr(>|t|)"] sd_treated <- sd(y_var[t_var == 1L]) sd_control <- sd(y_var[t_var == 0L]) round(c(lm_effect = lm_effect, lm_p = lm_p,         sd_treated = sd_treated, sd_control = sd_control), 3L) #>  lm_effect       lm_p sd_treated sd_control  #>     -0.011      0.954      2.505      1.108 fit_variance <- dr_date_test(y_var, t_var, x_var,   n_permutations = 299L, outcome_model = "zero", seed = 1L ) fit_variance #>  #>    DR-DATE Test #>  #> Statistic: 0.108574  #> P-value:   0.0033  #> N:         400  #> Perms:     299  #> Kernel Y:  rbf (bw = 1.563) #> ESS:       176.9

title: Scaling HSIC to large ensembles
text: exact kernel method stores n n Gram matrix iterates per permutation, memory time grow square sample size. Two standard low-rank factorisations replace matrix thin factor F K approximately F F', dropping cost order n m rank m much smaller n. nystrom_factor() implements Nystrom method Williams Seeger (2001): sample mm landmark observations, compute Gram matrix WW (mm mm) cross-Gram CC (nn mm), approximate K≈CW−1C⊤=FF⊤,F=Cchol(W)−1. K \approx C W^{-1} C^{\top} = F F^{\top}, \qquad    F = C \, \mathrm{chol}(W)^{-1}. works kernel data-dependent, landmarks drawn data. rff_features() implements Random Fourier Features (Rahimi Recht, 2007), available shift-invariant kernels, kernR means RBF kernel. Draw frequencies ω\omega normal covariance σ−2I\sigma^{-2} offsets bb uniform [0,2π][0, 2\pi]; feature map ϕ(x)=2/Dcos⁡(ω⊤x+b) \phi(x) = \sqrt{2 / D} \, \cos(\omega^{\top} x + b) gives K≈ΦΦ⊤K \approx \Phi \Phi^{\top} DD features. projection data-independent, random features apply point cloud bandwidth. hsic_test_nystrom() wires drop-accelerated independence test: method selects factorisation m sets rank feature count. returns kernel_test_result hsic_test().

what: Does the factorisation reproduce the kernel?
title: Scaling HSIC to large ensembles
text: synthetic cloud 80 points two dimensions, small enough exact Gram matrix can compared approximations directly. Reconstruction exact 80 80 Gram matrix factorisation.
code: set.seed(1L) n_check <- 80L x_check <- matrix(rnorm(n_check * 2L), n_check, 2L) kern <- kernel_spec("rbf", bandwidth = 1.0) k_full <- kernel_matrix(x_check, kernel = kern)  fac_ny <- nystrom_factor(x_check, kernel = kern, m = n_check - 1L,                          seed = 1L) k_ny <- tcrossprod(fac_ny$F)  fac_rf <- rff_features(x_check, kernel = kern, D = 1500L, seed = 1L) k_rf <- tcrossprod(fac_rf$F)  rel_err <- function(k_hat) {   sqrt(sum((k_full - k_hat)^2)) / sqrt(sum(k_full^2)) } recon <- data.frame(   method = c("nystrom", "rff"),   rank = c(ncol(fac_ny$F), ncol(fac_rf$F)),   rel_err = c(rel_err(k_ny), rel_err(k_rf)),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )

code: benchmark_hsic <- function(n, m, n_perm = 49L, seed = 1L) {   set.seed(seed)   x_bench <- rnorm(n)   y_bench <- x_bench + rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)   t_exact <- system.time(     res_exact <- hsic_test(x_bench, y_bench, n_permutations = n_perm,                            seed = seed)   )[["elapsed"]]   t_nystrom <- system.time(     res_nystrom <- hsic_test_nystrom(x_bench, y_bench, m = m,                                      n_permutations = n_perm, seed = seed)   )[["elapsed"]]   t_rff <- system.time(     res_rff <- hsic_test_nystrom(x_bench, y_bench, method = "rff", m = m,                                  n_permutations = n_perm, seed = seed)   )[["elapsed"]]   data.frame(     n = n, m = m,     method = c("exact", "nystrom", "rff"),     elapsed_s = c(t_exact, t_nystrom, t_rff),     p_value = c(res_exact$p_value, res_nystrom$p_value, res_rff$p_value),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) }  bench <- rbind(   benchmark_hsic(n = 250L, m = 40L),   benchmark_hsic(n = 500L, m = 60L),   benchmark_hsic(n = 1000L, m = 80L),   benchmark_hsic(n = 2000L, m = 100L) )

title: Which parameters change the shape of the output distribution?
text: variance-based Sobol index decomposes output variance contributions input, makes blind construction effect leaves variance . HSIC-Sensitivity Index Da Veiga (2015) replaces variance kernel dependence measure. normalised first-order index SjHSIC=HSIC(Xj,Y)HSIC(Xj,Xj)⋅HSIC(Y,Y)∈[0,1], S_j^{\mathrm{HSIC}}   = \frac{\mathrm{HSIC}(X_j, Y)}          {\sqrt{\mathrm{HSIC}(X_j, X_j) \cdot \mathrm{HSIC}(Y, Y)}}   \[0, 1], bounded like Sobol index, comparable across parameters, sensitive change conditional distribution output, including mean-preserving ones. hsic_sensitivity() computes every parameter every output, permutation p-value per pair Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across grid. total_order = TRUE adds total-order index Da Veiga’s complement form, TjHSIC=1−HSIC(X∼j,Y)HSIC(X∼j,X∼j)⋅HSIC(Y,Y), T_j^{\mathrm{HSIC}}   = 1 - \frac{\mathrm{HSIC}(X_{\sim j}, Y)}               {\sqrt{\mathrm{HSIC}(X_{\sim j}, X_{\sim j}) \cdot                      \mathrm{HSIC}(Y, Y)}}, measures contribution XjX_j directly plus every interaction takes part . total_order_ci = TRUE attaches pair-bootstrap percentile interval total-order index, total_order_test = "cond_perm" attaches conditional-permutation significance test . lhs_design() builds design; plot() .data.frame() render result.

what: A simulator built to separate the two questions
title: Which parameters change the shape of the output distribution?
text: synthetic stub four parameters, carrying one kind effect. mean_effect shifts mean, variance budget also sees. var_effect changes spread nothing else. tail_effect injects heavy-tailed component, changing shape without moving centre. inert nothing.
code: stub_apsim <- function(theta) {   n_row <- nrow(theta)   yield <- 1.5 * theta[, "mean_effect"] +     rnorm(n_row, sd = exp(theta[, "var_effect"])) +     theta[, "tail_effect"] * rt(n_row, df = 3) * 0.4 +     rnorm(n_row, sd = 0.05)   matrix(yield, ncol = 1L, dimnames = list(NULL, "yield")) }  set.seed(1L) bounds <- rbind(   mean_effect = c(0.0, 1.0),   var_effect  = c(-0.5, 0.5),   tail_effect = c(0.0, 1.0),   inert       = c(0.0, 1.0) ) design <- lhs_design(n = 600L, bounds = bounds, seed = 11L) yield <- stub_apsim(design)

title: Kernel-Based Causal Distributional Testing
code: library(kernR)  # Detect non-linear dependence (HSIC) set.seed(42) x <- rnorm(200) y <- x^2 + rnorm(200, sd = 0.3)  # quadratic relationship cor.test(x, y)$p.value            # Pearson: p = 0.85 (misses it!) hsic_test(x, y, seed = 1)        # HSIC:    p = 0.002 (detects it)  # Test for distributional treatment effect (DR-DATE) n <- 300 covariates <- matrix(rnorm(n * 2), n, 2) treatment  <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(0.3 * covariates[, 1])) outcome    <- treatment * rnorm(n, sd = 2) +       # treatment changes variance               (1 - treatment) * rnorm(n, sd = 1) +  # but NOT the mean               covariates[, 1]  t.test(outcome[treatment == 1], outcome[treatment == 0])  # p = 0.72 (blind) dr_date_test(outcome, treatment, covariates, seed = 1)    # p = 0.002 (sees it)

title: Aggregate-Likelihood Downscaling — aggregate_downscale
text: third downscaling method kernR, structurally different existing pair: kernel_downscale() (CME, Park-Muandet-Fukumizu-Sejdinovic 2013) – paired (coarse, fine) training data; supervised regression. dist_regression() (Szabo-Sriperumbudur-Poczos-Gretton 2016) – distribution--distribution mapping bag--points design. aggregate_downscale() (function) – aggregate observations + known aggregator + parametric latent prior. Used paired training data exists (coarse-grid observations) aggregation operator known (spatial averaging, temporal averaging, linear non-linear projection). Two computational paths, selected aggregator's class: Linear-Gaussian closed form (aggregator matrix ): prior component's posterior Kalman update; K_k = Sigma_k ^T (Sigma_k ^T + sigma_y^2 )^{-1}; mu_k|y = mu_k + K_k (y - mu_k), Sigma_k|y = (- K_k ) Sigma_k; posterior mixture weights reweight per-component evidence N(y | mu_k, Sigma_k ^T + sigma_y^2 ). Non-linear importance sampling (aggregator function): draw n_samples_per_component samples prior component, evaluate T(.), weight Gaussian likelihood N(y | T(x), sigma_y^2 ), recover posterior moments + reweighted mixture weights importance-weighted samples. Reports per-component effective sample size; warns stated floor. aggregate-likelihood / GMM-proxy direction shared companion proxymix Tier-2 stub proxymix::from_aggregate_likelihood(), targets problem prior-fitting side; function targets consumption side (inversion given fitted prior).

title: Aggregate-Likelihood Downscaling — aggregate_downscale
code: set.seed(1L) # Linear-Gaussian: spatial averaging of two adjacent cells. A <- matrix(c(0.5, 0.5), nrow = 1L) prior <- list(   means = list(c(0, 0), c(2, 2)),   covariances = list(diag(2L), diag(2L)),   weights = c(0.5, 0.5) ) fit <- aggregate_downscale(y = 1.0, aggregator = A,                            latent_prior = prior, sigma_y = 0.2) fit$posterior_mean #> [1] 1 1  # Non-linear: aggregator is sin of the sum. agg_fn <- function(x) matrix(sin(rowSums(x)), ncol = 1L) fit2 <- aggregate_downscale(y = 0.5, aggregator = agg_fn,                             latent_prior = prior, sigma_y = 0.1,                             n_samples_per_component = 300L, seed = 1L) #> Warning: aggregate_downscale(): per-component IS effective sample size fell below 10% of n_samples_per_component for component(s) 2 (ESS = 27.9). Increase `n_samples_per_component`, sharpen the prior, or consider a coarser aggregator if posterior is locally narrow. fit2$posterior_mean #> [1] 0.8567869 0.8729094

title: Emit a kernR verdict as an orchestra manifest — as_orchestra_manifest
code: mechanism <- function(theta, X, t) theta[3] + theta[1] * (1 - exp(-theta[2] * t)) set.seed(1L) n <- 60L nrate <- runif(n, 0, 200) yield <- 1.1 + 4.2 * (1 - exp(-0.018 * nrate)) + rnorm(n, 0, 0.25) post <- cbind(ymax = rnorm(100L, 4.2, 0.30),              rate = rnorm(100L, 0.018, 0.004),              y0   = rnorm(100L, 1.1, 0.15)) verdict <- taci_test(post, mechanism, X = matrix(1, n, 1),                      treatment = nrate, outcome = yield,                      n_perm = 99L, seed = 1L) m <- as_orchestra_manifest(verdict) m@summary$headline #> [1] "mechanism_consistent_effect [unverified]" m@summary$abstained  # FALSE: the posterior-adequacy gate passed #> [1] FALSE

text: x Numeric vector matrix. Treatment variable. y Numeric vector matrix. Outcome variable. z Numeric matrix, data.frame, data.table. Confounders. kernel_x Kernel specification treatment space. Default RBF median heuristic. kernel_y Kernel specification outcome space. Default RBF median heuristic. density_ratio Character. Method density ratio estimation: "logistic" (default), "ranger", "xgboost", "proxymix", "rulsif". "proxymix" backend fits Gaussian-mixture proxies joint product--marginals sample clouds via classical EM (Hoek & Elliott, 2024), giving parametric alternative NCE-based classifiers; useful multimodal densities classifier calibration unreliable. Requires proxymix package (>= 0.3.0). n_permutations Integer. Number permutations null distribution. Default 500. n_clusters Integer "auto". Number propensity clusters valid permutation cluster_id = NULL. Default "auto". split_ratio Numeric (0, 1). Proportion data training density ratio estimator. Default 0.5. alpha Numeric. Significance level. Default 0.05. seed Integer NULL. Random seed reproducibility. verbose Logical. Print progress. Default FALSE. cluster_id Optional vector length nrow(x) identifying external clusters (e.g. site, season, paddock, farm). supplied, permutation null built within-cluster reshuffling y, preserves cluster-level effects null. Coerced factor; test split inherits cluster assignment. result carries per-cluster stratified bd-HSIC alongside pooled statistic. permutation Character. Permutation scheme: "auto" (default) – cluster_id supplied, equivalent "within_cluster"; otherwise falls back k-means clustering propensity weights (original Hu/Sejdinovic/Evans scheme). "within_cluster" – requires cluster_id. Permutes y indices within clusters; preserves cluster-level effects. "naive" – unrestricted permutation across observations. Use independence within clusters plausible (rarely true ag-systems data). min_ess_fraction Numeric (0, 1) 0 / non-finite disable. ESS-floor reliability gate (added 0.0.0.9013): weighted-HSIC effective sample size min_ess_fraction * n_test, warning emitted result$ess_warning TRUE. default 0.1 (10%) conservative floor; tighten studies strict reliability requirements.

title: Backdoor-HSIC Test for Causal Association — bd_hsic_test
text: bd-HSIC test (Hu, Sejdinovic & Evans, 2024) tests whether treatment X causal effect outcome Y adjusting confounders Z via backdoor criterion. test works : Estimating density ratios w(x, z) = p*(x) / p(x|z) reweight observational samples interventional distribution. Computing weighted HSIC statistic X Y. Obtaining p-values via permutation Y within exchangeability clusters – propensity-similarity clusters default, external design clusters (site / season / paddock) cluster_id supplied. Hierarchical extension. design naturally clustered (multi-site agricultural trials, paddock x season factorial designs, patient x hospital data), supplying cluster_id activates within-cluster permutation: indices y reshuffled within cluster, preserving cluster-level effects null. safer default clustered data; naive permutation across clusters can inflate Type error cluster effects exist. Unlike PDS Double ML, bd-HSIC can detect non-linear causal effects (e.g., U-shaped relationships) treatment affects higher moments outcome necessarily mean. Small samples. minimum sample size 6 (train/test split must leave least two test observations weighted HSIC two propensity clusters). Small-N field trials supported, reliability guaranteed size alone: ESS-floor gate (min_ess_fraction) warn small poorly-overlapping sample yields weighted statistic dominated handful high-weight points.

title: Backdoor-HSIC Test for Causal Association — bd_hsic_test
text: density-ratio estimator now fit train split predicted held-test split via fit_density_ratio() + predict_density_ratio(). documented split_ratio honoured end--end four classifier / proxymix backends. 0.0.0.9013 sample-split leak warning therefore retired. RuLSIF, kernel-based closed-form backend, still uses estimate_rulsif() train/test split natively. fitted density-ratio model preserved result$density_ratio_fit callers want backend diagnostics (see ?fit_density_ratio Value; proxymix exposes BIC, AIC, log-likelihood, convergence per GMM).

title: Objective Causal Influence Range (threshold-free) — cir_objective
text: Reduces divergence-versus-lag profile single, threshold-free causal influence range (CIR) – effective horizon cause keeps informing estimate effect (Andreou et al. 2026, eqs. 8-9). Given relative entropy divergence lagged smoother (future effect included lag L) complete smoother (future included), divergence falls \(M\) lag 0 (filter, future) towards 0 L grows. subjective CIR tolerance \(\varepsilon\) \(\tau_\varepsilon = \inf\{L : D(L) \le \varepsilon\}\); integrating , $$\tau = \frac{1}{M}\int_0^M \tau_\varepsilon \, d\varepsilon   = \frac{1}{M}\int_0^{L_{\max}} D(L)\, dL,$$ second equality parts. result decorrelation-time analogue: lead time units lag, free cut-threshold.

title: Kernel Distribution Regression — dist_regression
text: Outer kernels supported. "linear": \(K(P_i, P_j) = \langle \hat{\mu}_{P_i},   \hat{\mu}_{P_j} \rangle =   \frac{1}{n_i n_j} \sum_{k,l} k(x_i^{(k)}, x_j^{(l)})\). "rbf": \(K(P_i, P_j) = \exp(-\| \hat{\mu}_{P_i} -   \hat{\mu}_{P_j} \|^2 / (2\sigma^2))\), embedding-space distance recovered inner Gram via \(\|\hat\mu_i - \hat\mu_j\|^2 = G_{ii} - 2 G_{ij} + G_{jj}\). Typical ag-systems use: paddock contributes bag soil-core measurements (variable depth, multiple cores per paddock); regression predicts paddock-level yield distributional shape soil profile. Distinct kernel_downscale() input distribution, fixed-length vector.

title: Doubly Robust Distributional Average Treatment Effect Test (DR-DATE) — dr_date_test
text: DR-DATE test (Fawkes, Hu, Evans & Sejdinovic, 2024) constructs doubly robust (augmented inverse-probability-weighted) estimators counterfactual mean embeddings Y(1) Y(0) reproducing kernel Hilbert space. arm \(\) augmented embedding $$\hat\mu_a = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i \tilde w_{,}   \bigl(k(y_i,\cdot) - \hat m_a(x_i)\bigr) + \hat m_a(x_i),$$ \(\hat m_a\) conditional mean embedding fitted arm \(\) \(\tilde w_{,}\) stabilised inverse-probability weights. statistic \(\|\hat\mu_1 - \hat\mu_0\|^2\) RKHS. Setting outcome_model = "zero" sets \(\hat m_a \equiv 0\) recovers inverse-probability-weighted statistic. Double robustness: test consistent either propensity model outcome (CME) model correctly specified. Cross-fitting (cross_fit = TRUE) makes hold flexible machine-learning nuisances removing -observation overfitting bias (Chernozhukov et al., 2018). Permutation null: reference distribution permutes treatment labels within propensity-score bins, holding fitted nuisances fixed. valid within-bin exchangeability treatment given (binned) propensity score; calibration degrades bins coarsen relative propensity variation inside . Key advantage: unlike DML TMLE test mean shifts, DR-DATE detects distributional difference including changes variance, skewness, shape.

Chernozhukov, V., Chetverikov, D., Demirer, M., Duflo, E., Hansen, C., Newey, W., & Robins, J. (2018). Double/debiased machine learning treatment structural parameters. Econometrics Journal, 21(1), C1-C68.

title: Doubly Robust Distributional Effect on the Treated Test (DR-DETT) — dr_dett_test
text: DR-DETT analogous DR-DATE focuses effect treated (ETT) rather average treatment effect. treated counterfactual Y(1) | T = 1 observed directly, control arm needs outcome model. control counterfactual Y(0) | T = 1 reconstructed augmented inverse-probability weighting, reweighting controls treatment odds \(e(x) / (1 - e(x))\) covariate distribution matches treated. outcome_model = "krr" control conditional mean embedding \(\hat m_0\) supplies doubly robust augmentation; outcome_model = "zero" returns inverse-probability-weighted statistic. requires one-sided overlap: P(T = 1 | X) bounded away 0 (necessarily 1), applies positivity fails control group.

title: Doubly Robust Distributional Effect on the Treated Test (DR-DETT) — dr_dett_test
text: Fawkes, J., Hu, R., Evans, R. J., & Sejdinovic, D. (2024). Doubly robust kernel statistics testing distributional treatment effects. Transactions Machine Learning Research.

title: Doubly Robust Distributional Effect on the Treated Test (DR-DETT) — dr_dett_test
code: set.seed(42) n <- 300 x <- matrix(rnorm(n * 2), n, 2) t <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(0.5 * x[, 1])) y <- t * rnorm(n, sd = 2) + (1 - t) * rnorm(n, sd = 1) + x[, 1]  result <- dr_dett_test(y, t, x, n_permutations = 200, seed = 1) print(result) #>  #>    DR-DETT Test #>  #> Statistic: 0.0342116  #> P-value:   0.0149  #> N:         300  #> Perms:     200  #> Kernel Y:  rbf (bw = 1.716) #> ESS:       102.2  #>

title: Fit a Density-Ratio Model — fit_density_ratio

title: Hierarchical Kernel Causal Test — hierarchical_test
text: clustered data (e.g., patients within hospitals, plots within farms), standard kernel tests may inflated type error observations within cluster independent. function decomposes test : Within-cluster: Average within-cluster test statistics (tests treatment effects within cluster). -cluster: Test cluster-level mean embeddings (tests treatment effects across clusters). combined statistic weighted sum, weights determined weight_method. Permutation performed within clusters preserve hierarchical structure.

title: Hierarchical Kernel Causal Test — hierarchical_test
code: # \donttest{ set.seed(42) n_clusters <- 20 n_per <- 30 n <- n_clusters * n_per cluster_id <- rep(1:n_clusters, each = n_per)  # Cluster-level random effects cluster_effect <- rnorm(n_clusters, sd = 1)[cluster_id] x <- matrix(rnorm(n * 2), n, 2) t <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(0.3 * x[, 1])) y <- 0.5 * t + cluster_effect + x[, 1] + rnorm(n)  result <- hierarchical_test(y, t, x, cluster_id,   method = "dr-date",   n_permutations = 100,   seed = 1 ) print(result) #>  #>    Hierarchical-DRDATE Test #>  #> Statistic: 0.0309451  #> P-value:   0.0099  #> N:         600  #> Perms:     100  #> Kernel Y:  rbf (bw = 1.822) #>  # }

text: First-order index (always computed): $$S^{HSIC}_j = \frac{HSIC(X_j, Y)}{\sqrt{HSIC(X_j, X_j) \cdot HSIC(Y, Y)}}$$ direct contribution X_j Y – analogous (equal ) Sobol first-order index. code: set.seed(1) chol2 <- chol(matrix(c(1, 0.9, 0.9, 1), 2L))  # Correctly correlated ensemble: calibrated jointly obs <- matrix(stats::rnorm(120L), ncol = 2L) %*% chol2 ens_ok <- matrix(stats::rnorm(4000L), ncol = 2L) %*% chol2 joint_coverage_test(ens_ok, obs, seed = 1L) #>  #>   Joint (multivariate) calibration diagnostic #>  #> Ensemble:    2000 draws x 2 dims; 60 held-out obs #> Pre-rank:    band_depth (dependence-sensitive) #> Coverage:    50%->53%   80%->80%   90%->88%  (nominal -> empirical rank band) #> Mean rank:   0.581 (0.5 = calibrated; <0.5 obs outlying, >0.5 obs central) #> Dispersion:  ratio = 0.883 (Var(rank)/(1/12)) #> Calibration: chi2 =    8, p = 0.5341 (rank histogram, 10 bins) #> Verdict:     calibrated (multivariate ranks consistent with uniform) #>   # Right margins, wrong dependence: ensemble independent, obs correlated. # coverage_test() passes; joint_coverage_test() catches it. ens_indep <- matrix(stats::rnorm(4000L), ncol = 2L) joint_coverage_test(ens_indep, obs, seed = 1L) #>  #>   Joint (multivariate) calibration diagnostic #>  #> Ensemble:    2000 draws x 2 dims; 60 held-out obs #> Pre-rank:    band_depth (dependence-sensitive) #> Coverage:    50%->37%   80%->62%   90%->77%  (nominal -> empirical rank band) #> Mean rank:   0.622 (0.5 = calibrated; <0.5 obs outlying, >0.5 obs central) #> Dispersion:  ratio = 1.225 (Var(rank)/(1/12)) #> Calibration: chi2 =   25, p = 0.0030 (rank histogram, 10 bins) #> Verdict:     REJECT -- jointly over-dispersed (observations too central) #>

text: Kernel-based hypothesis tests causal inference distributional treatment effects. Implements backdoor-adjusted HSIC (bd-HSIC) testing causal association, doubly robust kernel statistics (DR-DATE, DR-DETT) testing distributional treatment effects beyond mean shifts. Supports binary, continuous, mixed treatments, hierarchical/nested data structures, scales large datasets via Nystrom approximation random Fourier features. package depends 'PESTO' (GPL (>= 3)); kernR's sources released MIT licence, installed combination 'PESTO' combined work subject terms GPL (>= 3).

title: Kernel-Based Statistical Downscaling — kernel_downscale
text: Typical ag-systems use: coarse climate-grid inputs (e.g. monthly temperature, rainfall 25 km grid) -> fine-resolution outputs (paddock yield, biomass) time index. Train years coarse fine observed; predict fine outputs new coarse inputs. Compared linear regression baseline, kernel approach captures non-linear coarse-fine relationships without specifying functional form. Compared deep-learning downscalers, closed-form solution, uses orders--magnitude less data, carries interpretable kernel-bandwidth degrees--freedom knob.

title: Nystrom Low-Rank Kernel Factorisation — nystrom_factor
text: construction : Sample m landmark indices uniformly without replacement. Compute landmark Gram \(W = K_{mm}\) (m x m) cross-Gram \(C = K_{nm}\) (n x m). Stabilise: \(W_\epsilon = W + \epsilon \). Cholesky factor \(W_\epsilon = L L^\top\). Return \(F = C L^{-\top}\), \(F F^\top = C W_\epsilon^{-1} C^\top \approx K\). kernel_spec() supported. Bandwidth selection (median heuristic) performed full dataset landmark sampling.

title: Nystrom Low-Rank Kernel Factorisation — nystrom_factor
text: Williams, C. K. ., & Seeger, M. (2001). Using Nystrom method speed kernel machines. NeurIPS, 13.

title: Nystrom Low-Rank Kernel Factorisation — nystrom_factor

what: Relative Entropy Between Two Gaussians (the ACI causal metric) — relative_entropy
title: Relative Entropy Between Two Gaussians (the ACI causal metric) — relative_entropy
text: Computes Kullback-Leibler divergence \(\mathcal{P}(p, q) = \int p \log(p / q)\) two multivariate Gaussian distributions \(p = \mathcal{N}(\mu_p, \Sigma_p)\) \(q = \mathcal{N}(\mu_q, \Sigma_q)\). operational statistic Assimilative Causal Inference (ACI): p smoother posterior hidden cause (using future observed effect) q filter posterior (past ), non-zero value identifies hidden variable cause observed effect instant.

title: Relative Entropy Between Two Gaussians (the ACI causal metric) — relative_entropy
text: mu_p Numeric vector. Mean p (smoother posterior, ACI). sigma_p Covariance p: matrix, variance vector, scalar. mu_q Numeric vector. Mean q (filter posterior, ACI). sigma_q Covariance q: matrix, variance vector, scalar. Must positive definite (inverted).

title: Relative Entropy Between Two Gaussians (the ACI causal metric) — relative_entropy
text: single non-negative numeric: relative entropy \(\mathcal{P}(p, q)\).

title: Relative Entropy Between Two Gaussians (the ACI causal metric) — relative_entropy
text: closed form k-dimensional Gaussians $$\tfrac{1}{2}\left[\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_q^{-1}\Sigma_p)   + (\mu_q-\mu_p)^\top \Sigma_q^{-1} (\mu_q-\mu_p) - k   + \log\frac{\det \Sigma_q}{\det \Sigma_p}\right].$$ measure non-negative, zero two Gaussians coincide, asymmetric p q (divergence, distance). captures differences mean covariance invariant smooth invertible reparameterisation state. Covariance arguments accept k x k matrix, length-k variance vector (diagonal covariance), scalar (isotropic). reference covariance \(\Sigma_q\) must positive definite.

title: Relative Entropy Between Two Gaussians (the ACI causal metric) — relative_entropy
text: Andreou, M., Chen, N. & Bollt, E. (2026). Assimilative causal inference. Nature Communications 17, 1854.

title: Theory-anchored causal inference (TACI) mechanism-consistency test — taci_test
code: set.seed(1) n <- 80 nrate <- runif(n, 0, 200) yield <- 1.1 + 4.2 * (1 - exp(-0.018 * nrate)) + rnorm(n, 0, 0.25) post <- cbind(ymax = rnorm(200, 4.2, 0.30),               rate = rnorm(200, 0.018, 0.004),               y0   = rnorm(200, 1.1, 0.15)) mitscherlich <- function(theta, X, t) {   theta[3] + theta[1] * (1 - exp(-theta[2] * t)) } res <- taci_test(post, mitscherlich, X = matrix(1, n, 1),                  treatment = nrate, outcome = yield, n_perm = 100, seed = 1) print(res) #> TACI mechanism-consistency test #>   treatment: continuous (H0 baseline = 105.1) #>   statistic: unadjusted bd-HSIC #>   observed bd-HSIC: 0.06608 #>   H0 tail p-value:  0.010  (in tail: TRUE) #>   H1 central [0.05187, 0.07807]  obs at H1 pctile 0.35  consistent: TRUE #>   DECISION: MECHANISM_CONSISTENT_EFFECT #>   GROUNDING: [unverified] (mechanism provenance not declared -- verdict not grounded) res$grounding            # "[unverified]" -- no mechanism provenance declared #> [1] "[unverified]"  # Declaring mechanism provenance grounds the verdict (Independent Oracle # Principle). TACI builds its whole reference band from `mechanism`, which it # cannot itself check against reality; naming where the calibration came from # -- a citation, a fitted-model handle, or a PESTO manifest's run id and the # simulator version it was calibrated with -- moves `grounding` from # "[unverified]" to "grounded". res_grounded <- taci_test(   post, mitscherlich, X = matrix(1, n, 1),   treatment = nrate, outcome = yield, n_perm = 100, seed = 1,   mechanism_provenance = list(     run_id = "ies-2026-06-12-0042",     simulator = "APSIM NG 2024.6.7579",     reference = "Mitscherlich (1909) N-response form"   ) ) res_grounded$grounding   # "grounded" #> [1] "grounded"

title: kernR 0.2.0
text: nystrom_factor(): Nystrom low-rank kernel factorisation (Williams & Seeger, 2001). Returns n x m factor F F %*% t(F) \approx K [kernel_spec()]. O(n m^2) construction, O(n m) storage. Honours DESCRIPTION’s Nystrom claim. rff_features(): Random Fourier Features (Rahimi & Recht, 2007) RBF kernels. Returns n x D feature matrix Phi %*% t(Phi) \approx K. Data-independent random projection. Honours DESCRIPTION’s RFF claim. hsic_test_nystrom(): Drop-accelerated HSIC independence test via low-rank factorisation. method = "nystrom" (default) "rff". O(n m_x m_y) per permutation (vs O(n^2) exact test); verdict-equivalent hsic_test() moderate m. Uses biased HSIC estimator (form factors cleanly low-rank approximations). title: kernR 0.2.0
text: Initial development version. Kernel engine: RBF, Matern, linear, polynomial kernels RcppArmadillo backend. Bandwidth selection: Median heuristic (Rcpp), Scott’s rule. Base tests: hsic_test() (independence), mmd_test() (two-sample). bd_hsic_test(): Backdoor-adjusted HSIC causal association testing. dr_date_test(): Doubly robust distributional average treatment effect. dr_dett_test(): Doubly robust distributional effect treated. Hierarchical: hierarchical_test() nested/clustered data within/decomposition. Unified interface: kernel_causal_test() formula syntax y ~ treatment | confounders. Density ratio estimation: Logistic NCE via glm/ranger/xgboost; RuLSIF (kernel-based). Propensity scores: Cross-fitted estimation trimming diagnostics. Diagnostics: assess_overlap(), plot_weights(), effective_sample_size(). Vignettes: Quick start, bd-HSIC tutorial, DR-DATE/DETT tutorial, hierarchical data.
